summary.one_liner: pyenv is a shell-script tool for installing and switching between multiple Python versions (CPython, PyPy, and others) globally, per project, or per shell.
summary.what_it_does: pyenv installs multiple Python versions and lets you choose which one is active at the global, per-directory (.python-version file), or per-shell level. It also supports an environment variable override (PYENV_VERSION). It works by placing a directory of shim executables at the front of PATH that forward python, pip and similar commands to the selected version. Commands can search across several selected versions in a specified order, which the README notes helps when testing with tox. The README says it supports multiple distributions including CPython, PyPy, Stackless Python and Jython, and that most releases are built from source during installation. It is written in pure shell scripts and does not manage virtualenvs itself.
use_cases: install specific CPython or PyPy releases
test code across Python versions with tox
change the default system-wide Python for a user
run pip and python from a chosen interpreter
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash (automatic installer; URL not shown in the README text)
stack: shell scripts (Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, Nushell support)
notable: Shim-based design: adds a directory to PATH instead of requiring shell loading of functions
Can search several Python versions at once with fall-through to system Python
caveats: Does not officially support Windows; works only under WSL there, and installs Linux Pythons in that case
Most Python versions are built from source, so build dependencies must be installed first
Does not manage virtualenvs (pyenv-virtualenv is a separate plugin)
